design_notes: Requirement 1 was a data-only addition because the first version already had the ArgType interface from chapter note 6: the plug-in module defines RgbType (accepts/describe/expected) and a normal record, and the host calls registry.register_type + registry.register. No binder, spec validation or storage change was needed; only hubreg/demo.py gained one registration line.

The one ambiguity was how a non-JSON-Schema argument type should look in a tool schema. The requirement says schemas must describe the argument with type rgb, so RgbType.describe returns {"type": "rgb", "pattern": "^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$", "example": "#ff8800"}; controls needed no work at all because they read spec['type'] directly.

Requirement 2 could not be a pure plug-in because the API names reg.voice_phrases(); the smallest honest change was a two-line delegate in Registry. Phrase generation itself is a separate consumer module and holds only sentence templates, never per-action lists: the action name supplies verb and object, defaults/samples/enum values supply numbers and words, units are spelled out for speech, and the action's first doc sentence supplies a fallback phrase.
Natural phrasing from arbitrary action names remains heuristic (verb-first names read best); the generator only promises a non-empty, unique list, which is what the records can guarantee.

Requirement 3 was easy because option redirects already live in ArgSpecs and registration validates that their targets exist: the rename is one data edit plus {"target": "temperature", "temp": "temperature"}. The unknown-key-before-missing-argument check added earlier is what makes target=21 produce E_UNKNOWN_OPTION with fix 'temperature=<value>' instead of an unhelpful 'temperature is missing'.
The action result fields were left as ["target", "mode"] because the requirement renames the argument, not the result contract; temperature=21 runs and returns {'target': 21, 'mode': 'comfort'}.
chapter_feedback: Keeping every near-miss redirect in the records (note 4) is exactly what made the argument rename a data change rather than a binder change; the chapter's insistence that redirects are validated at registration also caught nothing only because the redirect target already existed.

The chapter's pluggable-argument-type note (note 6) made requirement 1 straightforward, but it does not say how a domain type should be rendered in a JSON tool schema, so choosing type 'rgb' versus 'string' plus a format/pattern was a guess.

The chapter has no fourth consumer that speaks natural language, and no guidance on generating prose from records; the voice consumer had to be invented, and its phrasing rules are heuristics rather than anything the pattern prescribes.

The chapter treats the registry as the single source but does not discuss whether a new consumer method on the registry counts as 'core'; I read 'core untouched' as binder/validation/storage untouched and added only the delegate the public API demands.

The chapter's warning that generated help is flat also applies to generated speech: the templates are correct and always current but read mechanically; good voice phrasing still needs written guidance.
